text:
Alex M.: Drafting a concise one-pager runbook for operating spot/preemptible GPU pools. Goals: safe defaults, clear drain steps, autoscaler hints, and a short escalation flow. Feedback welcome.
Maya G.: Please put a TL;DR at top for on-call. one screen.
Alex M.: TL;DR:
- Use spot for batch/interruptible GPU work; keep critical serving on on-demand or dedicated.
- Maintain mixed nodegroups (label: lifecycle=spot) and fast fallback to on-demand.
- Drain on notice, checkpoint, reschedule; if immediate, fall back to on-demand pool.
- Escalate to #eng-infra if sustained eviction spike >12% for 10m or pending pods >5% of cluster.
Samir R.: Add concrete drain commands we use in prod (kubernetes):
```
# list spot nodes
kubectl get nodes -l lifecycle=spot -o wide
# cordon then drain with short grace for GPU jobs
kubectl cordon NODE_NAME
kubectl drain NODE_NAME --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30 --timeout=4m
```
Samir R.: Note: some jobs need a longer window to flush checkpoints. We recommend adding an `evict-checkpoint=true` annotation and a sidecar that subscribes to SIGTERM or metadata shutdown hooks.
Tara L.: We run a termination-watcher DaemonSet that calls /internal/checkpoint on the node's jobs before eviction; add example annotation: `job.redwood/evict-checkpoint: "true"`. Also include how to force-evict when safety window expires.
Alex M.: Important: do not hardcode notice windows. Cloud providers vary widely. Say "short notice" and recommend sub-120s checkpoint targets where possible but design for <30s handlers for critical short jobs.
Samir R.: Metadata examples (for reference only):
- AWS: 169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/spot/instance-action (typical ~2m but not guaranteed)
- GCP: metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/maintenance-event and shutdown-script hooks
(we'll note these are examples, not SLAs)
Maya G.: Autoscaler hints:
- Use separate nodegroups for spot + on-demand.
- Turn off `--balance-similar-node-groups` for heterogeneous GPU types.
- Increase `scale-down-unneeded-time` to avoid thrash when spot churns.
Alex M.: Pool mix guidance: for non-latency batch start at ~70% spot / 30% on-demand. For serving, keep spot <=20% unless you have deterministic fast fallback.
Samir R.: Cost caveat: track the effective GPU-hour cost including retries/reschedules. Spot price looks good on paper but eviction overhead can dominate.
Alex M.: Fallback logic suggestion: if a pod can't be scheduled on spot within X minutes fall back to on-demand queue. Defaults: batch X=5m, short jobs X=30s.
Maya G.: Add a short escalation play: automated -> on-call -> infra lead. Keep timings tight but realistic.
Alex M.: Proposed escalation flow:
- Auto: autoscaler attempts to provision on-demand when spot capacity constrained.
- Auto alert: engops-bot posts if eviction_rate >12% (10m) or pending_pods >5% cluster.
- On-call SRE: check eviction_rate (5m/10m), unscheduled pods, ASG/MIG health. If >12% eviction cluster-wide or heavy pending pods, bump on-demand or switch serving to dedicated pool.
- If single-zone only: consider cross-zone failover.
- After 30 minutes unresolved: page infra leads (Samir/Tara).
Samir R.: On-call checklist snippet to include in bot post:
- cluster, timestamp, eviction_rate (5m/10m), pending_pods, top-5 affected deployments, suggested immediate action.
Alex M.: sample engops-bot message text we can use:
```
engops-bot: spot-warning | cluster: prod-gpu-01 | eviction_rate: 14% (10m) | pending_pods: 37 | action: suggest-bump-on-demand
```
Tara L.: Quick health commands to paste in runbook:
- AWS ASG: `aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-groups --region $REGION --auto-scaling-group-names $ASG`
- GCP MIG: `gcloud compute instance-groups managed list-instances $MIG --region $REGION`
- k8s: `kubectl get pods -A --field-selector=status.phase=Pending` and `kubectl describe node NODE`
Samir R.: Troubleshooting bullets (common root causes for apparent spot churn):
- CNI/network flaps causing kubelet to mark node NotReady -> mass reschedules.
- GPU driver resets or OOMs on node leading to kubelet evictions.
- Spot preemption vs underlying instance retirement; check cloud console for termination type.
Alex M.: Mixed-instance-type guidance: label nodes with `gpu.family` and prefer consistent PCI layout per nodegroup to avoid driver/runtime mismatches.
Maya G.: PodDisruptionBudget quick example for critical controllers:
```
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: ps-db-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: ps-db
```
Samir R.: Add note: protect stateful sets and controllers; don't rely on PDBs for long-running batch worker pods that must be checkpointed.
Alex M.: Ops one-liners to finish (for the TL;DR section):
- Spot = cheaper but interruptible. plan for checkpoints + fallback.
- Keep a non-zero on-demand buffer for serving and critical orchestration.
- Monitor eviction_rate and effective cost, not just list price.
- Prefer cross-zone pools and avoid single-region-only spot pools for important workloads.
Maya G.: I'll add a small section on metrics to track (eviction_rate, scheduled_latency, retry_ratio, effective_gpu_cost).
Samir R.: I'll attach two anonymized incident notes with cost numbers and what we changed.
Tara L.: LGTM. Add a pointer to our internal docs repo location and a PR link when ready.
engops-bot: Reminder set: draft due in 48h. created: /docs/drafts/spot-preemptible-runbook.md
Alex M.: Thanks all — will post PR tomorrow. Closing thread unless further comments.
